purpose: Phase 9 chapter rebuild active sequence. Prototype levels 01-15 remain as reference scenes but are no longer the active progression.

chapters.title: First Rescue
chapters.purpose: Teach automatic movement, exits, pit preview, and wall-turn behavior before abilities appear.

chapters.title: Holding the Crowd
chapters.purpose: Teach Blocker as the first player-controlled direction and crowd-control ability.

chapters.title: Building and Digging
chapters.purpose: Teach route construction: Builder creates temporary floor, Digger removes weak terrain.

chapters.title: Vertical Space
chapters.purpose: Teach long falls, parachutes, high walls, and routes split by height.

chapters.title: Combined Rescue
chapters.purpose: Use multiple abilities per level in full puzzle form, ending with a readable all-abilities prototype.

levels.title: Walk Home
levels.teaching_goal: Introduce automatic walking and the exit in a calm first level.
map_logic: One continuous floor leads directly to the exit.
No pit, wall, or ability is present.
The level confirms spawning, automatic walking, and rescue counting.
intended_solution: Do nothing.
All movers walk into the exit.
failure_logic: Failure should only happen if the time limit is too short or the exit is misplaced.

levels.title: Mind the Edge
levels.teaching_goal: Preview pits as visible danger without requiring an ability yet.
map_logic: The exit is placed before a clearly marked red pit.
The pit is visible as a future warning but should not be reached in normal play.
The player learns that red gaps are dangerous.
intended_solution: Do nothing.
All movers enter the exit before the pit.
failure_logic: If the exit route is missed in layout testing, movers continue into the visible pit.

levels.title: The Long Floor
levels.teaching_goal: Increase walking distance and spawned mover count while staying ability-free.
map_logic: A longer floor gives the player time to observe the queue.
Four movers spawn with a slower rhythm.
No ability or terrain hazard is required.
intended_solution: Do nothing.
Watch all four movers reach the far exit.
failure_logic: The only intended failure is a time-limit tuning issue.

levels.title: First Turn
levels.teaching_goal: Teach that movers turn around when they hit a wall.
map_logic: Movers spawn near the middle and initially walk right.
A red wall on the right turns them back left.
The exit is on the left side of the same floor.
intended_solution: Do nothing.
Movers hit the wall, turn left, and enter the exit.
failure_logic: Bad wall or exit placement can trap movers or make the route too slow.

levels.title: Stand Here
levels.teaching_goal: Introduce Blocker as a deliberate sacrifice that turns the crowd away from danger.
map_logic: Movers spawn on a single floor and initially walk right toward a marked pit.
The exit is safely placed on the left side of the same floor.
One blocker must stand between the spawn and the right-side pit.
intended_solution: Select Blocker.
Turn the first mover into a blocker before it reaches the pit.
The remaining movers turn left and enter the exit.
failure_logic: No blocker means the group walks into the right pit.
Blocking too late loses the rescue target.

levels.title: Lower Shelf
levels.teaching_goal: Teach using Blocker after a drop onto a lower platform.
map_logic: Movers start on an upper shelf and fall to a lower shelf.
The lower exit is left of the landing area.
The right side of the lower shelf leads to a marked pit.
intended_solution: Let the lead mover fall to the lower platform.
Apply Blocker on the lower platform before the right pit.
The remaining movers turn left into the exit.
failure_logic: Blocking on the upper shelf stops the intended route.
Blocking after the lower danger point loses too many movers.

levels.title: Two-Way Lesson
levels.teaching_goal: Introduce two available blockers on one floor with danger visible on both sides.
map_logic: A wide floor has marked danger beyond both ends.
The exit is left of the spawn area.
Two blockers are available so the player can experiment with controlling the group.
intended_solution: Use a blocker to prevent the group from walking into the first danger direction.
Use the second blocker only if needed to stabilize the group near the exit path.
Rescue three movers.
failure_logic: Spending both blockers away from the route can prevent enough movers from reaching the exit.
Ignoring either edge eventually sends movers into danger.

levels.title: Crowd Control
levels.teaching_goal: Summarize Chapter 2 by combining the two-floor drop with a tight rescue target: five movers, rescue four.
map_logic: Movers spawn on an upper shelf and fall to a lower shelf.
The lower exit is left of the landing area; the right side leads to a pit.
Five movers must be managed with only one blocker and zero extra deaths allowed.
intended_solution: Let movers fall to the lower platform.
Block the lead mover before the right pit on the lower floor.
The remaining four movers turn left and enter the exit.
failure_logic: Any mover falling into the right pit beyond the blocker makes rescue target impossible.
Blocking too late on the lower floor loses more than one mover.

levels.title: One Bridge
levels.teaching_goal: Introduce Builder: click a mover standing on the floor to create a bridge over a gap.
map_logic: A single gap separates the spawn floor from the exit floor.
No walls, no pits besides the gap itself.
The Builder button is the only ability visible.
intended_solution: Select Builder (auto-selected).
Click the lead mover before it reaches the gap.
The bridge spans the gap and all movers reach the exit.
failure_logic: No bridge means movers fall into the gap.
Building too late loses the lead mover.

levels.title: Bridge Twice
levels.teaching_goal: Use two Builder charges to cross two separated gaps.
map_logic: Three floor segments separated by two gaps.
Both gaps must be bridged.
The middle floor gives the player time to prepare the second bridge.
intended_solution: Bridge the first gap before the lead mover falls.
Bridge the second gap before the lead mover falls.
All three movers reach the exit on the rightmost floor.
failure_logic: Missing either bridge sends movers into a gap.
Spending both bridges on the same gap fails.

levels.title: Weak Wall
levels.teaching_goal: Introduce Digger: click a mover near a brown weak wall to remove it.
map_logic: A single continuous floor leads to the exit.
A brown diggable wall blocks the path before the exit.
The Digger button is the only ability visible.
intended_solution: Select Digger (auto-selected).
Click the lead mover when it approaches the weak wall.
The wall disappears and all movers continue to the exit.
failure_logic: Not digging the wall traps movers — they turn away from the exit.
Digging from too far away misses the wall and wastes the charge.

levels.title: Dig, Then Bridge
levels.teaching_goal: Combine Digger and Builder in sequence: open a wall, then bridge the gap behind it.
map_logic: A weak wall blocks the path; a gap sits between the wall and the exit floor.
Both abilities are visible and the player must switch between them.
The order matters: dig first, then bridge.
intended_solution: Select Digger, click the lead mover near the weak wall.
Select Builder, click the lead mover before the gap.
All three movers reach the exit.
failure_logic: Bridging before digging wastes the bridge on the wrong side of the wall.
Digging without bridging leaves the gap impassable.

levels.title: Build the Exit Route
levels.teaching_goal: Chapter 3 summary: hold the group with Blocker, dig open a wall, and bridge a gap to reach the exit.
map_logic: Movers spawn on the left and walk right toward a diggable wall.
Hitting the wall turns them back left toward a deadly pit.
The exit is on the far right on a raised platform, past the wall and an 80px gap.
Three abilities: one Blocker (stop the group before the left pit), one Digger (remove the wall), one Builder (bridge the gap).
intended_solution: Select Blocker, click the lead mover after it turns back from the wall.
The group turns right again. Select Digger, remove the wall.
Select Builder, bridge the gap to the exit platform.
Two movers reach the exit; the blocked mover is sacrificed.
failure_logic: Without Blocker, movers bounce between wall and pit until they fall in.
Without Digger, movers are trapped bouncing between blocker and wall.
Without Builder, movers fall into the gap before the exit platform.

levels.title: Soft Landing
levels.teaching_goal: Introduce Parachute: click a mover before a long fall to survive the drop.
map_logic: One mover spawns on a high platform and walks right toward a long drop.
A lower platform below catches the fall and holds the exit.
The fall distance exceeds the safe limit, killing the mover without a parachute.
intended_solution: Select Parachute (auto-selected).
Click the mover before it walks off the upper platform.
The mover drifts down safely and walks to the exit.
failure_logic: No parachute means the mover dies on landing.
Parachuting too late (after falling) still kills the mover.

levels.title: High Step
levels.teaching_goal: Introduce Climber: click a grounded mover near a tall wall to climb up to a higher platform.
map_logic: One mover spawns on a ground-level platform and walks right into a tall wall.
The wall is too high to walk over; turning around leads nowhere.
Above the wall, an upper platform holds the exit.
intended_solution: Select Climber (auto-selected).
Click the mover while it is on the ground near the wall.
The mover climbs up, lands on the upper platform, and walks to the exit.
failure_logic: No climb means the mover turns away from the wall and times out.
Clicking the mover while it is in the air has no effect.

levels.title: Hold the Landing
levels.teaching_goal: Combine Parachute and Blocker: save one mover on the dangerous right drop, then block to redirect another mover through the safe left route.
map_logic: Movers spawn near the center of an upper platform.
Right side: a long deadly drop to a lower platform with the exit.
Left side: two short safe drops (middle platform, then lower platform) that also reach the exit.
Blocker alone only rescues 1 (the third mover via the left route; the first dies, the second is sacrificed).
Parachute alone only rescues 1 (the first mover; the rest die at the right drop).
Both abilities together rescue 2.
intended_solution: Select Parachute, click the first mover before the right drop.
Select Blocker, click the second mover before the right drop.
The parachuted mover reaches the exit; the third mover turns left, takes the safe drops, and also reaches the exit.
failure_logic: Blocker alone: first mover dies at right drop, only third mover survives via left route (1 rescued, not enough).
Parachute alone: only one mover survives the right drop (1 rescued, not enough).
Parachuting the wrong mover or blocking too late loses the rescue target.

levels.title: Climb to Build
levels.teaching_goal: Combine Climber and Builder: climb a wall to reach an upper route, then bridge a gap to reach the exit.
map_logic: One mover spawns on the ground floor and walks right into a tall wall.
Above the wall, an upper platform has a gap before the exit segment.
Both Climber and Builder abilities are available; order matters.
intended_solution: Select Climber, click the mover near the wall to climb up.
Select Builder, click the mover before the gap on the upper platform.
The mover crosses the bridge and reaches the exit.
failure_logic: Using Builder before climbing wastes the bridge on the ground floor.
Climbing without bridging leaves the mover stuck at the gap.

levels.title: Split Heights
levels.teaching_goal: Chapter 4 summary: use Parachute on one mover to survive the left drop, and Climber on the other to reach the upper exit.
map_logic: Two movers spawn on a mid-level platform and walk right into a wall.
Climbing the wall leads to an upper platform with an exit.
Turning left at the wall leads to a 270px deadly drop; parachuting down is required to survive and reach the lower exit.
Each mover needs one different ability; both must survive.
intended_solution: Apply Climber to the first mover at the wall (or let it turn and apply Parachute).
Apply the remaining ability to the second mover before it reaches the wall or the left drop.
One mover climbs to the upper exit; the other parachutes to the lower exit.
failure_logic: Without parachute, any mover taking the left drop dies on impact (270px > 200px safe limit).
Using both abilities on the same mover leaves the other to die.
Missing either ability means only one mover survives (need both for rescue 2).

levels.title: Store and Release
levels.teaching_goal: Use Blocker to turn the crowd away from danger, then Digger to open the intended exit route.
map_logic: Movers walk right toward a visible pit.
The exit is left of a weak wall.
Blocker turns later movers left; Digger opens the weak wall.
intended_solution: Use Blocker before the right pit.
Use Digger near the weak wall.
Two movers reach the left exit.
failure_logic: Without Blocker, movers walk into the pit.
Without Digger, the left route remains closed.

levels.title: Over and Under
levels.teaching_goal: Climb to a high route, then dig through the weak wall before the exit.
map_logic: A tall wall leads to an upper platform.
A weak wall blocks the upper route.
intended_solution: Use Climber at the tall wall.
Use Digger on the upper weak wall.
failure_logic: No Climber leaves the mover on the lower route.
No Digger leaves the upper route blocked.

levels.title: Bridge the Drop
levels.teaching_goal: Survive a long fall with Parachute, then build from the landing platform to the exit platform.
map_logic: The mover falls from a high platform to a lower platform.
A lower gap requires Builder after landing.
intended_solution: Use Parachute before the fall.
Use Builder after landing to cross the lower gap.
failure_logic: No Parachute kills the mover.
No Builder leaves the lower gap impassable.

levels.title: Three-Step Route
levels.teaching_goal: Turn the group, dig open a weak wall, then bridge the final gap.
map_logic: A weak wall and final gap block the exit route.
Blocker protects the group from the opposite pit.
intended_solution: Use Blocker to hold the group.
Use Digger on the weak wall.
Use Builder on the final gap.
failure_logic: Wrong order wastes limited abilities.
Missing any required ability leaves the route incomplete.
